title: Why Product Teams Ship Features Nobody Uses (The Discovery Fix)
description:
The fastest way to waste a quarter: a stakeholder says "build X," and two weeks later an engineer is building X, with nobody checking whether X solves a real problem. This Short walks through the discovery workflow that stops solution-jumping: collect signals for a week or two, cluster them, validate the top clusters with interviews, and only then write the problem statement. Includes the analytics-team worked example from the lesson.

Source lesson(s):
- https://sigilipelli.github.io/product-manager-mastery-path/level-1/03-problem-discovery/

#Shorts

beats.narration: Here's how product teams ship features nobody uses. A stakeholder says build this, and two weeks later an engineer is building it. Nobody validated it's a real problem.
The fix is a discovery workflow. For one to two weeks, you just collect signals and commit to nothing.

display.heading: Step 1: collect signals, commit to nothing
display.subheading: Tickets, interview notes, metrics, sales and CS feedback

beats.narration: Then cluster the signals pointing at the same issue, and validate the top clusters with a few interviews or a data pull.

display.heading: Step 2: cluster, then validate
display.subheading: Confirm the top 2-3 clusters are real -- and roughly how big

beats.narration: One analytics team saw three unrelated signals. Instead of building notifications, they interviewed three at-risk accounts and found the real issue: users had no reason to return between report cycles.

display.heading: Worked example
display.subheading: Cluster first, interview, then name the actual problem

beats.narration: Only then do you write the problem statement, before anyone proposes a solution. Skip these steps and you build the loudest request, not the biggest one.

display.heading: Solutioning comes last
display.subheading: Write the problem statement before anyone pitches a fix
